per_prediction.description: Standard benchmark datasets for drug‑discovery GNN research (e.g., MoleculeNet, ChEMBL, PDBbind) are never used in the existing claims.
The literature contains virtually no empirical studies on molecular property prediction (e.g., solubility, toxicity, bioactivity) using graph neural networks.
There is a lack of methodological comparisons and baseline reporting across major GNN variants (MPNN, GCN, GAT) for drug‑discovery tasks.
There is a complete absence of work on protein–ligand interaction modeling and binding affinity prediction with GNNs.
No studies have applied graph‑based generative models (e.g., GraphVAE, MolGAN) for de novo molecular generation and optimization in drug discovery.
Evaluations are limited to generic claims; there is no real‑world, prospective, or longitudinal validation of GNN‑based drug‑discovery pipelines.
Transfer learning and fine‑tuning of pretrained GNN encoders for drug‑discovery applications remain unstudied.
